Ah, St. Louis style!

Previous gen Toyota Avalon:

 - Full size sedan so you can fit in it
 - Fairly luxurious, not Lexus luxury, but a lot better than a regular mid sizer
 - Reliable
 - Hybrid available if you want a bit more fuel economy. For it's size though, it's not bad

Only downside is that I wouldn't consider this car "fun" but it ticks all your other boxes. Although you did say you looked at the Impala and these cars are on the same level.

Someone else mentioned the Genesis sedan. It's pretty much like the Avalon, but more luxurious and rear wheel drive. RWD tends to suggest fun, but compared to the Avalon, you may be giving up a bit of reliability for it. That's not to say it will be bad, just IN GENERAL you can trust a Toyota. Also as a luxury car, you'd be paying a bit more for the equivalent year.

I'd test drive the Avalon and the Hyundai Genesis to see which you like more.

Btw the Matrix and the Pontiac Vibe are basically the same car. One brand might be cheaper, but they're both a Toyota underneath, so it's worth looking at.

Also in your price range, Mazda3 hatch and Focus hatch of similar years *I think* shared platforms, so you may want to look at these two as almost the same car. Don't quote me on that though, I couldn't find anything on google to confirm this.

Alternate take: You're probably gonna have to put up w/ super high mileage at that price point, if you are still going for the hatch.

Alternate alternate take: mini van :P

Wait what? What's a driving coach vs. instructor? 

Is this your first time learning?
Very cool... But how did the driver get out? I'm skinny af and I don't think I could make that.

Is this a thing? I usually order small fries, it's plenty enough for me, especially with a cheese burger. I felt like they gave a bit less than they normally do. I didn't feel as much as a fat fuck after eating everything, and that was with a milkshake from the Haagen Das as well =/
Isn't an instructor supposed to teach you then? What exactly did you pay for?

I think it sounds like you paid for an accelerated course or something. I had a friend that was considering one of those as she had previously did some lessons, but took a  break for a while due to financial issues.

I think if you can afford it, and assuming you want to learn soon you should be paying for lessons.

I'm gonna say jump lmao

Gas is expensive because you have to use premium. Maintenance is better than European brands, about $50 (around $50 - 60 for Lexus based on what I've heard from friends/coworkers) for my oil and filter changes which I do regularly according to the maintenance schedule.

You can find ways to make it cheaper by doing basic maintenance yourself, or for certain things like tires, you don't have to get at a dealership, they're just tires.

The sedan is practical, but I have the coupe. It's been fine so far, just maybe 2 or 3 times the trunk space wasn't enough... That's over 5 years of ownership.

I currently have a 2019 q50 as a loaner while I get some service done at the dealership. The q50 is okay, but I miss the G. A far far more engaging experience, even though it's less refined. Feels like a proper luxury/sport combo.

I don't know what happens at 100k miles, I got lucky when I bought mine with low mileage. I'm only at 62k and it's a 2010. I've not had any major issues yet.

Backup camera is nice. Cruise control (maybe) if you're getting an automatic and do lots of highway driving. 360 camera is good if you get a big vehicle, not gonna lie, of all the things I suck at when it comes to driving, it's parking lol.

Most driving assists, at least to me are things you shouldn't need because you pay attention to what you're doing and can drive in a straight line properly. That was sorta required for your license lol.

For non assists, android auto or apple car play. I've not actually used AC, but AA is so damn good, just to even have Google Maps in the dash. Makes infotainment systems look archaic by comparison.

Smaller stuff - power everything, keyless entry.
Subaru won't have the AWD advantage here anymore, the 2019 Mazda3 has AWD available.

> One thing the Subaru has going for it is the AWD system

Not for 2019 in this case, the 3 now is available with AWD.

Looks are great, but "nicer and smoother to drive" will outlast looks. I personally think the Mazda 3 is the better choice, especially now that it's available with AWD, which takes away the advantage that Subaru had.

Fair enough. I believe Mazda cx suv's had awd, so maybe it's a variant of that. But yeah I suppose if you want the best awd, Subaru wins in this case.

I think in most cases though, unless people are going off road, I would imagine any awd system to compliment good tires and driving carefully.

Previously you would have to choose between the 3 and the impreza, but if you wanted an awd system that was "okay enough" it makes the 3 a more competitive choice. But at the end of the day, if you want the best, the Subaru is the only choice.

Everyone else has covered some good cars, so I'll throw in something weird - Chevy SS.

2015's and up come with magnetic ride. 415hp/415tq from the LS3 6.2L V8 - same as in the Camaro. But it has 4 doors. If you don't mind something that looks like a Malibu, this is a pretty special car, if you'd like something unique.

You can get a decent 2015 auto for low to mid 30's. I test drove a 2015 auto recently, my final price was $33.7k OTD. Decided against it because I want a manual lol. But I would have jumped on that otherwise.

EDIT: To add a few more details. This is a Holden Commodore in Australia. In the US, people do a badge swap to get the Holden badges, and of course in Australia they do a Chevy badge swap :P They're both the same car. This car was made from 2014 - 2017, but I suggested a 2015 because of the Magnetic ride control - makes the car quite comfortable in touring mode, but a beast in performance mode. Brembo brakes work REALLY well too, seriously I was impressed. The car comes fully loaded with options (only options were transmission, color and sunroof anyway) and feels pretty premium (not too luxurious, but quite nice) when you don't want to drive like a hoon!
Q60 should be fine as long as it's not the new/current generation.
Along the same lines, Dodge have always been pretty silly, you have to like them for that. They put the Hellcat engine in an SUV... So why not put it in the minivan? xD
For real, my budget is $10k more than OP and I'm struggling lol

G37/Q60/Q50 (before the design refresh so 2008 - 2013). Hard to find one with a manual. Coupe might not be practical, I'd suggest taking your bike to the dealership when you test drive. But it does come in sedan form.

Maintenance isn't too bad, it won't be cheap like a non luxury brand, but it's a lot less than ze Germans ($50 is my oil change at the stealership, vs $100 is what I've heard for friends that have BMW's).

It also has comfort, bluetooth, usb and aux (depend on year) and a decent audio system with the upgraded Bose system.

Rubbish MPG tho, about 17 - 21 depending on how you drive. Drinks premium fuel as well.
Yeah minus that hood stripe that's a pretty good deal. It's only 1 state over too. I've never bought a car out of state though. Would be a fun drive back!
